## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## plugin:entire-engineering:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## Summary
- Pasted images/screenshots are externalized as raw binary blobs (`checkpoint/persistent.go`'s `writeAssets`) with no redaction call anywhere in the write path, and both OPF rewrite tree walkers explicitly skip the `assets/` subtree. This is a deliberate, defensible design choice — byte-level regex/entropy redaction can't safely touch binary image data without corrupting it — but `docs/security-and-privacy.md` didn't disclose it anywhere a user would actually look for it.
- The only related text was a low-level "JSONL skip rules" footnote framing the `type:image` skip as a false-positive-avoidance optimization for the text scanner, which reads as "we're careful not to over-flag images," not "images are never scanned by anything, ever."

## Change
- New, prominent "What Entire does NOT scan: pasted images and screenshots" section directly under "What Entire redacts automatically."
- Updated the "protecting sensitive data" checklist with an explicit "never paste a screenshot with secrets" bullet.
- Corrected the misleading JSONL-skip-rules footnote to point at the real explanation.

Docs-only change; no code behavior modified (deliberately — remediation depth like OCR-based scanning is a separate product decision, out of scope here).

## Test plan
- [x] Verified the disclosure accurately matches current code behavior (`writeAssets`, `manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go`)
- [ ] Full `mise run check` deferred to a follow-up pass (docs-only change, low risk)

--- a/docs/security-and-privacy.md
+++ b/docs/security-and-privacy.md
@@ -36,6 +36,16 @@ Entire automatically scans transcript and metadata content before writing it to
 
 Detected secrets are replaced with `REDACTED` before the data is ever written to a git object. Of the six secret-detection passes above, the scanner layer (pass 2) is configurable — see [Choosing secret-scanner engines](#choosing-secret-scanner-engines) below — while the other five are **always on** and cannot be disabled. User-defined rules (inline `custom_redactions` and rule packs) add a seventh secret-detection pass that only runs when configured.
 
+### What Entire does NOT scan: pasted images and screenshots
+
+**Every layer described above — all nine passes, including the opt-in PII and OpenAI Privacy Filter layers — operates only on transcript text. None of them ever inspect image content.**
+
+When you paste an image into an agent conversation (a screenshot of a terminal with a visible API key, a cloud console page showing a misconfigured resource, a photo of a document), Entire externalizes it out of the transcript and stores it as a **raw binary blob** under the checkpoint's `assets/` folder — completely unredacted, byte-for-byte identical to what you pasted. This blob is written to `entire/checkpoints/v1` (or the equivalent per-checkpoint ref on the `git-refs` backend) and pushed to your remote like any other checkpoint content.
+
+This is a **deliberate design choice, not a bug**: byte-level regex and entropy redaction cannot safely touch binary image data without corrupting the image, so Entire does not attempt it. There is currently no OCR pass, no vision-model PII/secret scan, and no gate that holds image assets back until reviewed — an image that enters a conversation ships to your checkpoint history exactly as pasted.
+
+**If you would not commit an image to your repository unredacted, do not paste it into an agent conversation.** This applies equally to a private repository — anyone with read access to checkpoint data can see it — and especially to a public one.
+
 ### Choosing secret-scanner engines
 
 Pattern matching (layer 2 above) is served by two independent scanner engines, each of which can be turned on or off:
@@ -362,6 +372,7 @@ If your AI sessions will touch sensitive data:
 
 - **Use a private repository.** This is the simplest and most complete protection. Committed checkpoints are then only visible to collaborators.
 - **Avoid passing sensitive files to your agent.** Content that never enters the agent conversation never appears in transcripts.
+- **Never paste a screenshot or image containing secrets or personal data.** Unlike text, pasted images are never scanned or redacted by any layer — see [What Entire does NOT scan: pasted images and screenshots](#what-entire-does-not-scan-pasted-images-and-screenshots).
 - **Review before pushing.** Checkpoints are written locally at commit time and pushed separately, so there is always a window to inspect them:
 
   ```fish
@@ -512,7 +523,7 @@ File an issue when the rule would benefit every Entire user (e.g., a major SaaS
 
 - **Best-effort.** Novel or low-entropy secrets (short passwords, predictable tokens) may not be caught.
 - **Filenames and binary data.** Secrets in filenames, binary files, or deeply nested structures may not be detected.
-- **JSONL skip rules.** Entire skips scanning fields named `signature`, fields ending in `id`/`ids`, structural-path fields (`filepath`, `file_path`, `cwd`, `root`, `directory`, `dir`, `path`), and objects whose `type` starts with `image` or equals `base64` — all to avoid false positives.
+- **JSONL skip rules.** Entire skips scanning fields named `signature`, fields ending in `id`/`ids`, and structural-path fields (`filepath`, `file_path`, `cwd`, `root`, `directory`, `dir`, `path`) to avoid false positives. Objects whose `type` starts with `image` or equals `base64` are also skipped by the text scanner — but this is not merely a false-positive optimization: images are never scanned by *any* layer, text or otherwise. See [What Entire does NOT scan: pasted images and screenshots](#what-entire-does-not-scan-pasted-images-and-screenshots) above for the full picture.
 - **Built-in PII patterns are US-centric.** `phone` matches North American (NANP) formats only — international formats, including E.164 numbers outside `+1`, are not detected. `address` matches the street line only; city, state, and ZIP/postcode are preserved. If you handle personal data from other regions, add `custom_patterns` for your locale rather than relying on the built-in categories alone.
 - **Custom PII patterns are user-authored.** Teams own the correctness of their `custom_patterns`. An invalid regex is logged and skipped, not enforced.
 - **Users are ultimately responsible** for reviewing what they commit and push. Redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee.

## Summary
- `collectJSONLReplacements`'s `shouldSkipJSONLObject` check (skip an entire subtree when an object's `"type"` field starts with `"image"` or equals `"base64"`) applied unconditionally anywhere in a transcript line's JSON tree — including inside a `tool_use` block's own `"input"` or a `tool_result`'s `"content"`/`"output"`, fields whose shape is controlled by whatever tool declared them. For an MCP tool, that's a third party, not Entire's transcript writer.
- A tool call argument or response deliberately shaped as `{"type":"base64", ...}` hid an arbitrarily large sibling secret behind a single spoofed tag, from every scanning layer (regex, entropy), then shipped unredacted to a pushed branch.
- Threads a `toolPayload` flag through the walk, set once the recursion enters a `tool_use` block's `input` or a `tool_result` block's `content`/`output`, sticky for all descendants. `shouldSkipJSONLObject` is honored only outside `toolPayload`. Genuine externalized image assets (pasted screenshots) are message content blocks, not tool call input/output, so the documented, intentional image-asset skip (`docs/security-and-privacy.md`) is unaffected.

## Deliberately scoped — what this does NOT touch
`shouldSkipJSONLField`'s id/signature-suffix and path-family skips are **not** touched here. Several are load-bearing for real built-in tool calls (Read/Grep's own `file_path`/`path` arguments live inside `tool_use.input`), and narrowing them without full visibility into every supported agent's wire format (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini, Factory Droid, Pi each have their own shape) risks reintroducing the false positives they exist to prevent. I verified this against real fixture data (`cmd/entire/cli/transcript/compact/testdata/*.jsonl`) and confirmed e.g. Copilot's own hook payload legitimately nests `sessionId`/`cwd` inside an `input` object unrelated to tool calls. Flagging this as follow-up rather than guessing at a broader fix under time pressure.

- Genuine reproduction (`TestCollectJSONLReplacements_ToolPayloadCannotSpoofImageSkip`): a real secret wrapped in a spoofed `type:base64`/`type:image` object inside both a `tool_use.input` and a `tool_result.content`, asserting it is now caught.
- **Mutation-verified**: temporarily reverted the `toolPayload` gate, confirmed the test fails (both evasion shapes reproduce exactly as described, secret silently unredacted), then restored the fix.

## Summary
- Every agent `entire investigate` spawns runs with sandbox/approval checks unconditionally disabled — Claude Code's `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` and Codex's `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` are not conditioned on any flag.

Turning `entire investigate`'s ordinary use into a prompted confirmation would just train operators to reflexively accept it — this closes the "totally silent" gap without adding friction to the tool's core function. Happy to revisit the UX call if a maintainer feels this should gate harder.

## Summary
- `CleanupPushedShadowBranches` runs automatically after every successful push, with no confirmation, and trusted `shadowBranchPattern` (`entire/<7+ hex>(-<6 hex>)?`) directly for deletion eligibility.
- The bare, unsuffixed half of that pattern (`entire/<hex>`, no dash) is also a plausible human branch-naming convention — short-SHA branch names are an ordinary convention, and Entire reserves no documented namespace. A branch like `entire/1234567` with no session-state entry (a hand-created branch never has one) was silently, permanently force-deleted (`git update-ref -d`, no merge-check) the next time `entire` pushed anything in that repo.
- Adds `isAutoDeletableShadowBranch`, requiring the worktree-hash suffix that `checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit` always appends (even for the main worktree — `HashWorktreeID` hashes an empty worktree ID to a real 6-hex value, never an empty one). That shape is the actual, unspoofable-in-practice output of the one function that mints shadow branches — a much stronger ownership signal than bare name matching.
- Wired into both `CleanupPushedShadowBranches` (the eligibility filter) and `DeleteShadowBranchesIfUnchanged` (its own independent guard, defense-in-depth).
- Old-format branches remain listed and deletable through the interactive `entire clean --all` path, where a human sees the branch name and confirms before anything is deleted — only the unattended, no-confirmation path is narrowed here.

## Verification
- Real-git reproduction test (`TestCleanupPushedShadowBranches_HumanBranch_Survives`): plants a human-plausible `entire/abc1234` branch alongside a genuine orphaned shadow branch, confirms only the genuine one is deleted.
- **Mutation-verified in two steps**: reverting only the eligibility-filter gate still passed (the independent `DeleteShadowBranchesIfUnchanged` guard caught it — confirms the defense-in-depth is real, not just written); reverting both gates together reproduced the original bug exactly (2 branches deleted instead of 1, including the human one); restored the fix and confirmed the full targeted test suite (every pre-existing shadow-branch/cleanup test) passes with no regressions.
- `go build ./cmd/entire/...` passes.

## Summary

content.text:
Reviewed all ten. All of them fail "Entire Gates" for the same non-code reason — the `approvals` gate is at 0/1, waiting on you. Ignore that signal.

## Merge as-is (4)

**#2224 — OAuth cross-host redirect.** The strongest of the set. Real bug (Go's client strips sensitive *headers* on cross-host redirect but copies the POST body, where `subject_token` lives), fixed at the one choke point instead of per-caller, genuine two-server repro, mutation-verified, and it's the only PR where `mise run check` actually ran. Full CI green.

**#2225 — cross-repo checkpoint identity.** CI green. I probed the live cell to confirm the new checks can't false-positive: `/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/checkpoints/…` returns `repo_full_name: "entireio/cli"` and `checkpointId: "01M1FVHFTZ3HC4TATD1JYMSE4M"` — both present, exactly cased. The repo-ID-as-`repo_full_name` fallback is covered by its own accepting test.

**#2231 — `investigate fix` following an untrusted path.** Real read-primitive, and the fix routes through the already-validated resolver. I checked the two paths are the same file, so nothing is lost for paused/cancelled runs: `resolveDocPaths` builds `commonDir/investigations/<runID>/findings.md` (`cmd.go:897`) and `StateStore` resolves `<dir>/<runID>/findings.md` (`state.go:222`). CI green.

**#2233 — sandbox-bypass notice.** Small, non-blocking, drives the real command in test. Nit only: it hardcodes two agents' flag names, which will drift as agents are added.

## Merge and fix forward (3)

**#2227 — image redaction disclosure.** Docs-only, and the security conclusion is right — I confirmed `writeAssets` (`persistent.go:1875`) blobs `a.Data` with no redaction call. But the new section describes externalization into `assets/` as what happens, and it's opt-in: `redaction.externalize_images` defaults false (`settings.go:1780`), and the doc never mentions the setting. In the default config images stay *inline* and are skipped by `shouldSkipJSONLObject` instead. One sentence to fix.

**#2230 — shadow-branch cleanup ownership.** Correct and honestly argued. I verified the load-bearing claim: `DeleteShadowBranchesIfUnchanged` has exactly one production caller (`cleanup.go:189`), so `clean --all`'s interactive path is genuinely unaffected. CI green. The disclosed trade-off is real though — genuine legacy bare-format shadow branches now accumulate instead of being auto-cleaned. Your call whether an `entire/<hex>` human collision is likely enough to be worth that.

**#2232 — session-state clear race.** The part that matters is right: `CondenseSessionByID`'s `clearAfter` now clears inside the locked closure, and that's the routine-traffic race. Two things to fix after:
- The body's claim that this covers `entire doctor` is wrong. `doctor.go:415` calls the **package-level** `strategy.ClearSessionState` (`session_state.go:892`), still completely unlocked. The `(*ManualCommitStrategy).ClearSessionState` wrapper it *does* harden has zero production callers.
- Lint is red — 2 trivial errcheck hits on `_ =` in the new test. That one blocks merge.

## Need changes (2)

**#2234 — redaction skiplist scoping. Don't merge.** I measured it against main with a realistic Claude Code `tool_result` carrying an image (`Read` on a `.png`, or an MCP screenshot tool):

| | main | #2234 |
|---|---|---|
| 64KB image | 87,580 → 87,580 bytes, intact | 87,580 → **15,845 bytes, `REDACTED`** |
| 2MB image | 8.7 ms | **2.72 s** (313×) |

The walk now hands base64 image payloads to the entropy scanner, which flags and destroys them — exactly what CLAUDE.md warns about ("redaction would otherwise flag and destroy the high-entropy base64"; "base64 is the pathological input for the entropy layer"). It hits the default config, since `externalize_images` is off and images stay inline. The evasion it closes is real; the fix is too broad. Direction: skip the known image *payload leaves* (`data`, `source.data`) rather than un-skipping the whole subtree — that removes the hide-a-sibling-secret hole without feeding base64 to the scanner. Also 1 errcheck hit at `redact.go:1015` (`blockType, _ := val["type"].(string)`).

**#2226 — shadow-branch migration race.** Right problem, right approach, not ready:
1. **Lint red, and one is a real test bug.** `runGitOut` calls `require.NoErrorf` and is invoked from inside the writer goroutine — `t.FailNow()` off the test goroutine is undefined behavior, so this can hang CI rather than fail. Plus 2× `exec.Command`→`CommandContext` and an unused `repo` param.
2. **That unused `repo` param is the tell.** Repository identity moved from the caller's `*git.Repository` to `state.WorktreePath` + subprocess cwd. `WorktreePath` can be empty (`manual_commit_session.go:248`, `:390` both branch on `== ""`), and `cmd.Dir = ""` runs against the process cwd — the wrong-repo hazard CLAUDE.md documents. Meanwhile `manual_commit_session.go:503` still uses `repo` one line above the call.
3. **`readRefHash` fails open.** Any `*exec.ExitError` reads as "branch doesn't exist", but `git rev-parse --verify` also exits 128 for "not a git repository", dubious ownership, and corruption. A broken directory therefore reports "nothing to migrate", advances `state.BaseCommit`, and orphans the branch. Needs exit-1 vs 128 classification.
4. Minor: `MigrateShadowBranchRef` self-deadlocks on `oldBranch == newBranch` (same flock twice). Unreachable today — the caller guards prefix collisions at `manual_commit_migration.go:110` — but the exported API should guard itself.
5. Worth thinking about: migration now runs inside `MutateSessionState` (`manual_commit_git.go:48`) and takes two blocking flocks with no timeout, lengthening the critical section under the session gate. Relevant to Codex's 3s session-end budget.

One pattern across the set: eight of ten say "`mise run check` deferred," and four of those are exactly the ones with red lint. Worth telling Suhan the deferral isn't buying anything.

I can write these up as PR review comments if you want — say the word, since I haven't posted anything.

content.text:
Two inline comments, both from `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` on a "Lite"-effort review. No human comments.

**1. "`attackerSawToken` is unsynchronized, will race under `-race`, can make the assertion flaky"** — this is the one Copilot blocked approval on, and it's wrong on the consequence. I ran it: 600 executions under `-race` (`-count=200 -cpu=1,4,8`), zero DATA RACE reports. Also zero with the guard reverted.

The reason is structural: when the guard works, the attacker handler **never executes**, so there's nothing concurrent to race on. And with the guard removed, the server→client response delivery gives the detector enough happens-before that it still doesn't fire. So it won't red CI and it isn't flaky. The pattern is fragile in principle, and `atomic.Bool` is a one-line change worth taking just so the next bot doesn't re-flag it — but it's not a reason to hold the PR.

**2. "The comment says the copy avoids overriding a redirect policy, but the code does override it"** — correct, and slightly more substantive than Copilot frames it. A caller who *had* set their own `CheckRedirect` would have it silently ignored for this call, while the comment reads as though it were preserved. No caller does today — I checked both construction sites (`cell_data_api.go:354`/`360` and `cross_juris_transport.go:558`), neither sets `CheckRedirect` — so it's wording only. Reword to what the copy actually buys: don't mutate a client instance callers may share.

**What Copilot missed, and it's worth more than either comment:** `require.Error` at `oauth_test.go:88` is followed by `assert.False(t, attackerSawToken)` at line 89. `require` aborts the test, so on a regression line 89 never runs — in my mutation run only line 88 fired. The test's headline claim, "the attacker never sees the token," is therefore decorative: it can only ever be evaluated on the happy path, where the handler didn't run anyway. Making line 88 an `assert.Error` turns it load-bearing.

Verdict unchanged — still merge. All three are one-liners if you'd rather fold them in first.

Pushed to `security/oauth-redirect-token-leak` as `f71135cd9`. CI is rerunning; I've got a monitor on it and will report when it settles.

What went in:

**1. The doc comment (Copilot was right).** It claimed the shallow copy avoids "overriding any redirect policy already set on" the client — the opposite of what happens. Now it says what the copy actually buys (the caller's shared instance isn't mutated) and states the precedence explicitly, with a note that a caller needing its own policy here should get a same-host-preserving hook rather than have the guard removed.

**2. `atomic.Bool` for `attackerSawToken`.** Kept the finding from my last message in the comment: it doesn't race in practice, and the reason is that the handler never executes while the guard works. It's atomic so a future regression surfaces as a failed assertion rather than a race report.

**3. The dead assertion — one correction to what I told you.** I said `assert.Error` was the fix. It isn't: `testifylint`'s `require-error` rule is enabled in this repo and rejected it. Reordering does the same job — the leak check now runs *before* `require.Error`, so the abort can't skip it.

Verification:

- Mutation check, guard removed: **both** assertions now fire, leak check first. Before, only the error assertion did — confirming that check really was decorative.
- Package green 150× under `-race` across `-cpu=1,4,8`.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean on the formatted tree (I re-ran lint after the reorder), plus `go build ./...` and `go vet`.
- The production change is comment-only — I verified the `oauth.go` diff contains no non-comment lines.

Nothing about my earlier verdict changes: this was already the strongest PR of the ten, and it's ready barring your approval on the gate.
